ing: pierced with a knife (or 2 tbsp lime juice)
st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic, cinnamon, cardamom, turmeric, coriander and cumin. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the chicken, dried limes and [[2 tsp]] salt, and turn the chicken to coat it in the masala.
Pour in [[4 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate. Check it reached 165°F (74°C) inside. Keep it warm.
Add the rinsed rice to the broth, stir once, and bring back to a boil. The pot should hold about [[4 cups]] of liquid, so add a splash of water if short.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest the rice off the heat for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the rice on a platter topped with the chicken. The dried limes can be broken open and stirred in for a sour flavor.

ing: plus extra to serve (ghee works too)
st: Put the drained wheat, chicken, cinnamon stick and [[8 cups]] water in a large heavy pot.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then cover and simmer on low for 60 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and check it reached 165°F (74°C). Let it cool 10 minutes, then shred the meat and discard the skin and bones.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot with [[2 tsp]] salt.
Keep simmering on low, uncovered, for 90 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. Add hot water if it gets too thick.
Remove the cinnamon stick. Stir hard with a wooden spoon or mash with a potato masher until the wheat and meat blend into a thick, smooth porridge.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter and cook 5 more minutes.
Spoon into bowls, make a small well in the center, and add a spoonful of melted butter.
Dust with [[1 tsp]] ground cinnamon and serve hot.
Whisk the flour, cornstarch, yeast, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, cardamom and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Pour in [[1 cup]] warm water and the saffron with its soaking water. Beat for 2 minutes into a thick, sticky, stretchy batter.
Cover the bowl and let the batter rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes until bubbly and doubled.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Stir the batter once. Scoop a small amount with a wet spoon and push it off with another wet spoon into the oil, making balls the size of a walnut.
Fry 5 or 6 balls at a time for 3 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Repeat with the rest, keeping the oil at 350°F.
Pile the dumplings on a plate and drizzle generously with [[0.5 cup]] date syrup. Serve warm.
In a large bowl, mix [[0.5 cup]] yogurt, [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice, minced garlic, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, and all the spices with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Add the chicken thighs and turn until every piece is coated.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Heat a large skillet or grill pan over high heat with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Cook the chicken in a single layer, in two batches if needed, for 6 minutes per side until charred and cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then slice it thinly against the grain.
Warm the pita in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
Spread [[2 tbsp]] garlic sauce on each pita, add the chicken and a few pickles.
Roll up tightly, wrap the bottom in foil or paper, and serve.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the vermicelli and stir for 3 minutes until lightly golden.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water, the saffron with its soaking liquid, and [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 8 minutes until the noodles are soft and most of the water is absorbed.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] sugar and the rose water, if using. Cook 2 more minutes, then cover and keep warm.
Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt and [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[1 tbsp]] butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Pour in the eggs and cook for 3 minutes, until set on the bottom and lightly golden, then flip and cook 1 minute more until fully cooked with no runny egg.
Spoon the sweet noodles onto a plate and top with the thin omelette. Serve warm.
Whisk the flour, yeast, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, cardamom and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add the eggs, [[1.5 cups]] warm milk and the saffron with its water. Whisk into a smooth, thin batter.
Cover and let the batter rest in a warm place for 45 minutes until bubbly.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat and brush lightly with butter.
Pour in about [[0.25 cup]] batter and spread it into a thin round.
Cook for 2 minutes until the top is full of small holes and the underside is golden. Flip and cook 1 minute more.
Repeat with the rest of the batter, buttering the pan between pancakes and stacking them on a plate under a towel.
Serve warm with cheese and a drizzle of [[0.5 cup]] date syrup.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb in two batches, about 5 minutes per batch.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon and [[2 tsp]] salt for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until jammy.
Pour in [[5 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 60 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer 15 minutes, then add the zucchini and simmer 10 minutes more until all vegetables are soft.
Check that the lamb is tender and cooked through to at least 145°F (63°C).
Lay the torn bread in a wide serving dish.
Ladle plenty of the hot broth over the bread so it soaks, then top with the lamb and vegetables. Serve right away.

ing: white fish fillets (such as cod or tilapia)
st: Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, cumin, turmeric and pepper and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the fish and [[4 cups]] water with [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until the fish falls apart.
Sprinkle in [[0.5 cup]] flour a little at a time, stirring constantly so there are no lumps.
Lower the heat and cook for 25 minutes, stirring often and mashing the fish with the back of a spoon, until thick and porridge-like.
Beat hard with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes until smooth, adding a splash of water if too stiff.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] butter, taste for salt, and serve hot in a shallow bowl with a pool of melted butter on top.
